newsitem.title: UK: Wall St reversal, rate fears hit European stocks, dollar.
newsitem.headline: Wall St reversal, rate fears hit European stocks, dollar.

text.p: A sharp reversal on Wall Street and concern that interest rates might have to rise undermined European stock markets in early trading on Tuesday.

The recently buoyant dollar also lost some of its gloss after Germany's six leading economic research institutes said a slight monetary tightening was possible if growth in money supply stayed above target levels.
Market analysts said investors were unlikely to be too adventurous ahead of a run of U.S. economic data this week.

The latest readings of the health of the world's biggest economy start with third-quarter employment cost and consumer confidence figures later in the day and culminate in October payrolls data on Friday.

The Dow Jones industrial average, barometer of the New York stock market, the world's biggest, was up around 26 points as its London counterpart closed on Monday. But it ended 35 points lower as investors braced for the flood of economic news.
Just as the Dow, surrendering more than the amount it regained on Friday, ended below the key 6,000 level, London's FTSE 100 index slipped below its own 4,000 landmark.

"We are looking at a 60-point reversal in the U.S. from where we left it last night and despite the (Northern Electric takeover) bid yesterday, London wasn't very happy about itself," said one senior London share trader.
"With huge economic numbers from the U.S. on Friday, a monetary meeting here and U.S. elections next week, people are not going to be buying this market," another trader said.
In Frankfurt, shares were depressed by uncertainty over interest rates, Wall Street's decline and a weaker dollar, which made less pleasant news for exporters.
The German institutes said current interest rates were appropriate but the Bundesbank should not shrink from tightening policy if M3 money supply growth continued to overshoot targets.
French shares also opened lower amid bond market worries that the German central bank might have to increase its key interest rates, which would have a knock-on effect in other European currencies.

In earlier Asian trading, the dollar had hit a new 42-month high of 114.88 yen against a Japanese currency weakened by a search by Japanese investors for higher-yielding investments abroad and political uncertainty after recent elections.

Japanese Finance Minister Wataro Kubo said the yen's current movements reflected fundamentals and the situation did not warrant special attention. U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin had said he was not concerned about the dollar's rise.
But the U.S. currency headed lower against both the mark and yen after the German institutes' comments since any move to boost German rates would tend to strengthen the mark.
"Outside of a weak yen, you haven't got a strong dollar environment at the moment," said Chris Tinker, chief economist, treasury at Standard Chartered Bank in London.
Even before the latest comments from Germany, the U.S. currency's progress against the mark had lagged its ascent against the shaky yen amid fading hopes for lower German rates.
CURRENCIES AT 1040 GMT
The dollar was trading around 1.5125 marks and 113.70 yen versus 1.5207 and 114.26 in late European business on Monday.
Elsewhere, the South African rand received a fresh mauling, hitting a new all-time low of 4.69 against the dollar.
STOCKS AT 1040 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was down 28.2 points at 3,997.1.
Germany's DAX index was 20.50 lower at 2,683.33, surrendering most of Monday's gains. In Paris the CAC-40 index lost 24.33 to 2,126.06.
Tokyo's Nikkei 225 rose 72.67 to 20,958.08.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $382.35 an ounce, down from Monday's London close of $383.35. Silver eased two cents to $4.91.
